h2: Plumber & Pool Service in Denpasar – Bali Fix
intro: Denpasar's tight lanes, older drainage lines and busy shop-house plumbing mean something is always giving way. Bali Fix handles everything from a burst pipe in Renon to a green pool in Sesetan — one WhatsApp message gets you sorted.

sections.h3: What Breaks Most Often on PDAM Mains
sections.text: Mains supply drops without warning across Renon, Sidakarya and Panjer, so your tank, float valve and pump become the real lifeline. In shop-houses and small offices on shared PDAM lines, toilets clog under heavy daily use, while electric or gas water heaters in family homes develop limescale that kills performance. Bali Fix clears blockages, replaces worn valves, services heaters and keeps pumps running — send photos over WhatsApp for a quote.

sections.h3: Neighbourhoods We Cover Across the City
sections.text: From Kesiman villas to Denpasar Barat offices, we work the full city. The most common calls? A blocked drain after a long lunch service, a leaking septic line under an older house, or a pool turning cloudy because nobody cleaned it during a business trip. Villa managers in Sesetan and Panjer often book regular pool service plus quarterly plumbing checks so small issues never become flooded ceilings.

sections.h3: Wet Season: When City Drains Push Back
sections.text: Once the wet-season rains set in, Denpasar's ageing drains simply can't keep up. Water backs through floor gullies into ground-floor rooms, especially on narrow lanes where the city pipe is undersized for the volume above. If you've seen brown water rising from your drain after a storm, don't wait — a blocked or broken sewer line needs clearing before the next downpour. Bali Fix handles septic jetting, sewer repairs and emergency water removal across all six neighbourhoods.

sections.h3: Pool Care & Water Heaters for Family Villas
sections.text: Family homes in Renon and Sidakarya typically run one electric or gas heater alongside a small pool, both of which need monthly attention to avoid scale build-up and algae blooms. We clean, balance chemicals, swap worn filters and service pump motors as part of a regular package. For one-off fixes — a cracked tile, a stuck skimmer, a heater that won't ignite — just snap a photo and send it on WhatsApp; pricing depends on the job.

faq.q: Do you cover all of Denpasar including the western suburbs?
faq.a: Yes — Renon, Sidakarya, Panjer, Sesetan, Kesiman and Denpasar Barat are all within our working area, so a single WhatsApp message reaches us regardless of which side of town you're on.

faq.q: PDAM cut off my water again. What should I check first?
faq.a: Start with your float valve and tank level, then confirm the pump is actually running. If those look fine but pressure is still low, there's likely a leak further along the line — send us a photo of the setup and we'll point you in the right direction.

faq.q: How often should a villa pool be serviced in Bali's climate?
faq.a: At minimum every two weeks for cleaning and chemical balancing, because humidity and dust keep introducing contaminants between visits. A monthly equipment check (pump motor, filter, skimmer) catches wear before it becomes an expensive repair.
